Diop Breaks the Deadlock The contest began with a cagey opening as both teams sought to establish dominance in midfield. However, it was Fulham who struck first in the 20th minute. Following a well-worked attacking sequence, Issa Diop rose highest in the box to power a commanding header into the back of the net. The early goal gave the Cottagers a deserved lead and forced Newcastle to become more adventurous in their approach. As the first half progressed, Newcastle looked to respond through set-pieces delivered by Lewis Hall and Bruno Guimarães , but the Fulham backline remained resolute. Rodrigo Muniz nearly doubled the advantage in the 28th minute with a sharp header of his own, only to be denied by a comfortable save from Nick Pope . Cairney’s Moment of Magic The second half saw a flurry of tactical changes and an increase in physical intensity. Newcastle 's Bruno Guimarães and Yoane Wissa both saw yellow as the referee worked to maintain control. The decisive moment arrived in the 80th minute, courtesy of a brilliant substitution. Harry Wilson , having recently entered the fray, played a short corner to Tom Cairney . The experienced midfielder unleashed a stunning left-footed strike from outside the box that flew past Nick Pope to make it 2-0. In the closing stages, Newcastle pushed forward in search of a late lifeline, with Sean Neave seeing a shot blocked by a determined Jorge Cuenca . Despite a missed chance by Alex Iwobi and late bookings for Antonee Robinson and Cuenca , Fulham managed the game professionally. The final whistle confirmed a solid 2-0 victory for the London side, providing a significant boost of confidence as they continue their pre-season preparations.
